question: Do the run-time selected x86-64 SIMD tiers (eight-window SSE2/AVX2/AVX-VNNI-INT8 products, SSE2/AVX2 rotation rows) and the SSE2 pyrDown speed up the stable core's fixed-scale match on x86-64 with bit-identical outputs, without slowing the Apple arm64 build?

commits.after: 869502729de13b74a98bffde202461ec413691bf (c74913c tiers + 8695027 SSE2 pyrDown; 7506003 only changes two experiment tests)

sources: git archive of each commit's cpp-core (docs excluded), unpacked into fresh directories on each machine

pc.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 9 285K (8 P-cores + 16 E-cores, no SMT; cpuid: AVX2, FMA, AVX-VNNI, AVX-VNNI-INT8, no AVX-512)
pc.toolchain: MSVC 19.44.35207 (VS Build Tools 2022 17.14), CMake 3.31.6, Ninja, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, no /arch flag (x86-64 SSE2 baseline), pure core (no OpenCV)

builds.after-auto: default (FPM_X86_MAX_ISA=VNNI_INT8; picks AVX2+VNNI-INT8 on this CPU)

pc.affinity: every timing driver is started with `start /affinity C03C02` (P-cores 1,10-13,22,23; CPU 0 and all E-cores excluded); fpm_cli children inherit it

mac.script: formal-mac.sh (archived); refuses to run while a side-session timing lock exists; records uptime/load

inputs: the 17 compare_versions cases as 8-bit PGM copies from export_fixture_pgm.py; manifest.json sha256 3a539fec058b4f42e613c074a8fcb0f697ae2ca671cd76645bc8a23b6cd8e64f; the PC copies are checked against it before any run

gates.ctest: every PC configuration (before, after-auto/avx2/sse2/scalar, both ASan builds) and both Mac builds pass ctest; the Mac research build at 8695027 passes ctest
gates.identity_pc: check_backend_identity.py --pgm-dir with libraries before, auto, avx2, sse2, scalar (SIMD and scalar backends each): 17 cases x 4 modes x 10 = 680 runs, zero runs different from before/scalar
gates.identity_mac: the same tool with before and after on arm64: 272 runs, zero different
gates.cross_platform: every case/mode reference output (binary64 hex) of the PC equals the Mac's
gates.mutants: x86_mutants.py: 20 compiled mutants of the SSE2/AVX2/VNNI-INT8 kernels, rotation rows and SSE2 pyrDown, each built under the tier cap that runs it; all must be killed by fpm_core_test, and the unmutated and restored trees must pass

timing.tool: benchmark_backend_ab.py --rounds 8 (round 0 warm-up discarded), alternating order, fresh fpm_cli process per run, --pgm-dir; metric fpm_cli match_ms (excludes decoding and template learning)
timing.no_drops: no run is dropped or repeated; a failed run is reported as failed

decision_rule: Adopt when every gate above passes, the PC default before/after geometric-mean ratio (after/before over the 17 per-case medians) is below 1, and the Mac default ratio is at most 1.02. Speeds are otherwise reported, not gated.
not_formal: the pilot (x86_pilot.cpp), the counter-instrumented profiles and the preliminary run_cli_cases.py runs were made before this registration on uncommitted trees; they chose the variants and are archived as selection evidence only
profiling: a counter-instrumented copy of 8695027 is profiled after the formal runs, separately; its times are not formal
